maya: Heads-up — canary showing a sudden uptick in formatting / table extraction hallucinations on model-x:awq-int8-v2 deployed to shared-pool canary.
maya: Eval delta vs hosted fp8 baseline: F1 on TableX down from 0.92 -> 0.84, hallucination rate +9%. Quick numbers attached.
maya: snippet from failing case:
```
input: |\n  | id | name | amount |\n  | 1  | Acme | $1,200 |\nexpected: {"rows": [{"id":"1","name":"Acme","amount":"1200"}]}
awq-int8 output: {"rows": [{"id":"1",""name":"Acme","amount":"$1,200"}, {"id":"2","name":"TOTAL","amount":"1300"}]}
```
sam: ugh. saw similar on other table extract tests yesterday but thought it was batch shape noise.
li: is this only on shared-pool? any repro on dedicated/private runs?
maya: quick check: dedicated with same model build (awq-int8-v2) seems much better — F1 0.90. So could be pooling/batching interaction.
jonah: interesting. could be kv-cache boundary or inter-request batching merging prefix tokens. Did you check batch shapes? what batch sizes/seq lengths in canary?
maya: canary traffic had bursts of 1-8 concurrent small reqs (seq len 80-150). Dedicated run we forced batch=1 / no dynamic fusion.
sam: reminds me of the "interleaved-request prefix bleed" we saw in 1728500123. but filenames aside, could be AWQ's reorder with continuous batching.
maya: I reran local eval harness with controlled batching and saw the regression only when continuous_batching=true and max_batch_size>=4. With continuous_batching=false AWQ-int8 matches fp8 baseline.
li: ok that points to runtime interaction. what about GPTQ and FP8 variants under same conditions?
maya: quick table:
- fp8-baseline: F1 0.92 (batching either)
- gptq-int8: F1 0.91 (continuous batching ok)
- awq-int8-v1: F1 0.86 (bad on continuous)
- awq-int8-v2 (current canary): F1 0.84 (worse)

jonah: so AWQ variants degrade with continuous batching. could be quant ordering / kv pointer arithmetic. we should run a micro-benchmark to isolate kv cache alignment.
sam: also check per-channel vs per-tensor quant mode; awq uses per-channel by default but our conversion script had a fallback flag on canary build.
maya: yes — discovered canary build used quant-mode=per-tensor due to an earlier conversion bug. mixing per-tensor + continuous batching seems to amplify tokenization/escape issues.
li: that could explain formatting noise (dollar signs, escaped pipes). per-tensor loses representational fidelity for some columns.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary created for model-x:awq-int8-v2 at 2026-03-20T14:02Z on cluster shared-pool-3. ID c-993.
maya: action items I propose:
- disable canary (rollback) until we confirm (ops)
- run micro-bench: kv-cache alignment test across batch sizes 1..8 (eng-runtime)
- rebuild awq-int8 with quant-mode=per-channel and run canary in shared-pool (eng-ml)
- add a targeted eval suite for TableX escape cases to canary gating (qa/devex)

sam: I'll attach a quick repro script for kv alignment and the eval subset.
sam: repro gist:
```
# run_kv_alignment.sh
for b in 1 2 4 8; do
  ./run_eval --model model-x:awq-int8-v2 --batch $b --continuous_batching true --dataset tablex_edgecases.json
done
```
maya: ran that locally, results show error rate jumps at batch>=4 consistently. logs:
```
batch=1: errors=3/1000
batch=2: errors=5/1000
batch=4: errors=42/1000
batch=8: errors=47/1000
```
li: good repro. Jonah/eng-runtime can you triage kernel selection and pointer offset math? maybe an index overflow in fused attention when quantized per-tensor.
jonah: putting it on my board. first step: reproduce with ASAN build and compare kernel calls between batch=1 and batch=4.
ops-bot: ops: rollback initiated for canary c-993 by li at 2026-03-20T14:20Z :warning:
maya: thanks. will post updates after micro-bench runs and a rebuilt quant conversion.
sam: if per-channel rebuild fixes it, we should enforce conversion flag in CI and add a canary smoke check for table escapes.
li: agree — also add a canary param to disable continuous batching for new quant builds until validated.
maya: adding follow-up: schedule a short postmortem doc with examples and exact prompts for the oncall + devex. tagging @devex to add to canary gating checklist.
jonah: noted. I'll try to get initial ASAN traces in the next 6h. :mag:
maya: thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
